name: The rotated crossing is the crossing
summary: Bending two legs of the fermionic crossing around (rotating it by a quarter turn) gives the crossing.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

Rotating the crossing by a quarter turn, by bending one input into an output with a cap and one output into an input with a cup, gives the crossing again. In the planar W-calculus of Carette et al. this is one of the axioms that let the fermionic swap be treated almost like an ordinary swap.
